findings.claim: handoff.pack described a complete plan as though it were always read at the tdd stage, so the first pack written at the review stage told its reader to run the regression and the coverage.
findings.failure_scenario: A reviewer opens the pack at record 22, reads that the regression is what is left, and runs one the journal recorded at 20; a reviewer who trusts it returns a ticket whose tdd stage is complete.
findings.resolution: The regression clause is appended only at the tdd stage, with a test for each reading. Recorded at 23, returned at 24, RED 26, GREEN 27.

findings.claim: _section charged the character budget for an 'and N more' line it discarded when no entry fitted, so remaining went negative and every later section was dropped.
findings.failure_scenario: A journal with long decisions fills the budget, the graph answers section is offered a negative remaining and writes nothing, and the next session asks codegraph and repowise questions this one already recorded answers to. The pack does not say a section was dropped.
findings.resolution: A section that does not fit charges nothing and only what was written is subtracted, with two tests. RED 26, GREEN 27.

findings.claim: The pack was written and read back with the locale's encoding while its bytes are compared against the sha256 the handoff record carries.
findings.failure_scenario: On a runner whose locale is not UTF-8, a non-ASCII ticket title raises UnicodeEncodeError as a session tries to hand off, or writes bytes status --brief reads back differently and reports as drift. The skill source in this repository already carries non-ASCII characters.
findings.resolution: Both calls name encoding='utf-8', with a test that reads cli.py, because the failure needs a locale a unit test must not change for the whole process. RED 26, GREEN 27.

findings.claim: kpi.slices read only the most recent tdd advance, so a ticket that was returned understated the slices it proved and inflated its cost per slice by the same factor. The first delivery of this ticket wrote 1 proven of 3 planned into its own kpi.json.
findings.failure_scenario: Every returned ticket reports fewer proven slices than it worked, and output tokens per slice divides the whole ticket's tokens by the rework slices alone: on this ticket, three times too large. Read at a sprint gate, the figure says slices cost three times what they cost and that two planned slices were never proved, which is the opposite of what the journal shows. It is the divisor in the KPI this ticket exists to create, so the error would have been read as the definition.
findings.resolution: Proved now sums the slices of every accepted tdd record, the way red_before_green already reads them, so a re-proved slice counts again because it was worked again and proven above planned is rework showing up. Found by reading the kpi.json the first delivery wrote, with the pull request open; the receipt over 4d6f30bc was voided with harness reopen at record 35, which is what SEEN-093 built it for. RED 36 (1 against 2, and 90,000 against 45,000 on the cost), GREEN 37, regression 39 over 402 tests.
